scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user reboots their PC and now cannot get an IP address. Other
PCs that were already up keep working (their existing leases are
still valid). Newly connected devices on any internal VLAN time
out waiting for DHCP. Existing TCP sessions are unaffected.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 dhcpd (ISC DHCP server)
Mechanism: r1 is the central DHCP server for every internal
  VLAN (A-PC, A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi).
  DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as unicast to 10.0.0.76 (R1's
  loopback). With dhcpd dead, requests reach r1 but get no
  reply. Existing leases keep working until their lifetime
  expires; renewals start failing after lease-time/2.
Localization: r1
Root cause: dhcpd is not running on r1
Fix: restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is the isc-dhcp-server (dhcpd) daemon on r1 being killed after
initial lab startup. r1 hosts the single centralised DHCP server for all
internal VLANs; its loopback address 10.0.0.76/32 is the relay target
configured on both active relay agents (dswa1 and dswb1). When dhcpd is not
running, every DHCP DISCOVER that a relay agent unicasts to 10.0.0.76
receives no response, so any client sending a DISCOVER (newly booted or
re-connected device) simply times out. Devices that already hold a valid
lease continue to communicate normally because they do not need to re-run
the DORA exchange until lease expiry — exactly matching the reported symptom.

At first observation, `systemctl status isc-dhcp-server` showed
`inactive (dead)` and no dhcpd process existed. The /etc/default/isc-dhcp-server
file was correctly configured (INTERFACESv4="eth0 eth1 lo") and the dhcpd.conf
was unmodified (md5sum identical to the hostlab copy), ruling out a
configuration corruption. When the service was started manually it launched
immediately and printed "ignore stale pid file /var/run/dhcpd.pid", confirming
that dhcpd had run once (during the r1.startup script, which does invoke
/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server start) and was subsequently killed, leaving a
stale PID file. The relay path from dswa1 to 10.0.0.76 is fully functional
(ICMP round-trip 0.6 ms). The design choice to run relay only on dswa1/dswb1
is intentional (dswa2.startup explicitly marks itself as non-relay).

Root cause: the isc-dhcp-server process on r1 was killed after lab
initialisation, removing the sole DHCP server from the network.

Corrective fix: run `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server start` on r1 (already
applied during diagnosis; dhcpd pid=214 is now listening on UDP/67).

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies r1 as the affected device (the central DHCP server).
The report explicitly names the isc-dhcp-server (dhcpd) on r1 as the failed component and describes its termination and restart.
The diagnosis explicitly contrasts working existing leases (no DORA until expiry) with new/rediscovering clients timing out, satisfying the required distinction.
Proposes starting the isc-dhcp-server on r1 (equivalent to the expected restart), which restores the DHCP daemon and fixes the fault.

The agent's logs show dhcrelay running on the DSWs, r1 had the loopback 10.0.0.76, dhcpd was not running at first (stale pid evidence) and was successfully started manually and then listened on UDP/67; the writeup's claims follow from these observations. The investigation covers the essential checks (server process, stale PID/startup, relay config, connectivity, config integrity) though it doesn't fully prove why dhcpd was killed.
